title: A Healthy Walk Begins on the Street
title_ja: 健康的な散歩は街づくりから始まる

source_links.title: CDC: Increasing Physical Activity Through Community Design

fact_notes: 背景となる考え方は添付の資料で確認。本文と練習問題は新規制作。例示した人物・学校・活動は架空の説明用設定。

sentences.en: Doctors often encourage people to exercise, but personal motivation is not the only factor affecting physical activity.
sentences.ja: 医師は運動を勧めることが多いですが、個人のやる気だけが身体活動を左右する要因ではありません。

sentences.en: A person may want to walk every day yet live beside a busy road without a safe sidewalk.
sentences.ja: 毎日歩きたくても、安全な歩道のない交通量の多い道のそばに住んでいる人もいます。

sentences.en: Others may live far from shops, parks, or public transportation and need a car for ordinary trips.
sentences.ja: 店や公園、公共交通から遠く離れ、日常の移動に車が必要な人もいます。

sentences.en: However, good community design can make active travel safer and more convenient for many residents.
sentences.ja: しかし、よい街づくりは、多くの住民にとって身体を動かす移動を安全で便利にできます。

sentences.en: This idea shifts attention from individual choices to the environments in which those choices are made.
sentences.ja: この考えは、個人の選択から、その選択が行われる環境へと注目を移します。

sentences.en: Health can therefore be influenced by streets as well as by hospitals and exercise classes.
sentences.ja: したがって健康には、病院や運動教室だけでなく、街路も影響します。

sentences.en: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention discusses how community design can support physical activity.
sentences.ja: 米国疾病対策センターは、地域の設計が身体活動をどう支えられるかを論じています。

sentences.en: For example, a well-maintained sidewalk can help people reach a bus stop without entering moving traffic.
sentences.ja: 例えば整備された歩道があれば、車の流れに入らずにバス停へ行けます。

sentences.en: Streetlights and safe crossings may make an evening walk feel more comfortable.
sentences.ja: 街灯や安全な横断場所は、夕方の散歩をより安心できるものにするでしょう。

sentences.en: Benches can be especially useful for people who need to rest during a longer journey.
sentences.ja: ベンチは長い移動の途中で休む必要のある人に特に役立ちます。

sentences.en: A shaded path may also be easier to use during hot weather than a road without protection from sunlight.
sentences.ja: 日陰のある道は、日差しを遮るものがない道よりも暑い時期に使いやすいかもしれません。

sentences.en: These changes do not force everyone to walk; they simply make walking a more realistic option.
sentences.ja: こうした変更は全員に歩くことを強制するのではなく、徒歩をより現実的な選択肢にします。

sentences.en: Designing for accessibility means considering residents whose needs are not always easy to see.
sentences.ja: 利用しやすさを考えて設計するとは、外からはわかりにくい住民の必要を考慮することです。

sentences.en: A path that works for a healthy adult may present barriers to a wheelchair user or someone with limited vision.
sentences.ja: 健康な大人には使いやすい道でも、車いす利用者や視力に制約がある人には障害となるかもしれません。

sentences.en: In addition, a crossing that feels safe in daylight may be difficult to use after dark.
sentences.ja: さらに昼間は安全に感じる横断場所も、暗くなると使いにくい場合があります。

sentences.en: Planners can learn more by speaking with people who actually travel along the proposed routes.
sentences.ja: 計画担当者は、提案された道を実際に使う人々と話すことで、より多くを学べます。

sentences.en: Such conversations can reveal problems missing from a map or a short official report.
sentences.ja: そうした会話から、地図や短い公式報告書では見えない問題が明らかになることがあります。

sentences.en: A useful design should be evaluated by how well different people can use it, not only by its appearance.
sentences.ja: よい設計は見た目だけでなく、多様な人々がどれほど利用できるかで評価されるべきです。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, building one sidewalk does not guarantee better health for an entire community.
sentences.ja: それでも歩道を一つ作るだけで地域全体の健康が改善するとは限りません。

sentences.en: People also need time, useful destinations, and confidence that they can move around safely.
sentences.ja: 人々には時間、役立つ目的地、安全に移動できるという確信も必要です。

sentences.en: A school could ask students to record places where they feel safe or unsafe on their journeys.
sentences.ja: 学校は、生徒に通学途中で安全・危険と感じる場所を記録するよう求められます。

sentences.en: Students might compare these observations with maps and discuss improvements that would help more residents.
sentences.ja: 生徒は観察記録と地図を比較し、より多くの住民の役に立つ改善を話し合えるかもしれません。

sentences.en: As a result, a lesson about walking can become a lesson about fair access to public spaces.
sentences.ja: その結果、徒歩についての授業は、公共空間を公正に使うことについての授業にもなります。

sentences.en: A healthier city is not just a place where people are told to walk, but one that makes safe movement possible.
sentences.ja: より健康的な街は、歩くよう言われるだけの場所ではなく、安全な移動が可能な場所です。

questions.prompt: What does the passage mainly suggest?
options: Personal motivation is the only factor in exercise.
Community design can make healthy movement safer and more accessible.
Every road should be closed to cars.
A new sidewalk guarantees perfect health.
questions.explanation_ja: 街づくりが健康的な移動の機会に関わるという主張です。

questions.prompt: Why may some people need a car for every ordinary trip?
options: Shops and public transport may be far away.
They dislike all forms of exercise.
questions.explanation_ja: 施設や交通機関が遠いことが理由です。

questions.prompt: Which features can improve an evening walk?
questions.explanation_ja: 街灯や安全な横断場所が役立つ例です。

questions.prompt: Why are benches useful on walking routes?
options: Some people need places to rest.
questions.explanation_ja: 長い移動中に休憩が必要な人がいるためです。

questions.prompt: Who might face barriers on a path that others find comfortable?
options: A wheelchair user or person with limited vision.
questions.explanation_ja: 車いす利用者や視力に制約のある人が挙げられています。

questions.prompt: Why should planners speak with local travelers?
options: They may reveal problems missing from maps.
They always know every future event.
Planners should avoid official reports completely.
questions.explanation_ja: 実際の利用者だけが気づく障害があるためです。

options: Ease of use by people with different needs.
The price of a bus ticket.
The number of roads in a city.
The length of a medical report.
questions.explanation_ja: accessibilityは多様な人が利用しやすいことです。

questions.prompt: What could students record during school journeys?
options: Places where they feel safe or unsafe.
The entire history of the town.
questions.explanation_ja: 通学途中で安全・危険と感じる地点を記録します。

questions.prompt: Why is a single sidewalk not enough?
options: Health also depends on destinations, time, and safety.
All health outcomes come from hospitals alone.
questions.explanation_ja: 移動目的地、時間、安全性など複数の条件が必要です。

questions.prompt: Why does the writer contrast being told to walk with having safe routes?
options: To emphasize that practical conditions support healthy choices.
To say only doctors can design streets.
To recommend walking on dangerous roads.
questions.explanation_ja: 行動を指示するだけでなく実行できる環境が必要と結論づけます。

grammar.focus: in which those choices are made
grammar.explanation_ja: 前置詞＋関係代名詞in whichがenvironmentsを修飾します。

grammar.focus: than a road without protection from sunlight
grammar.explanation_ja: 比較級easier thanで道を比較しています。

grammar.focus: that works for a healthy adult
grammar.explanation_ja: 関係代名詞thatがpathを修飾しています。

grammar.focus: not just a place where people are told to walk, but one that makes safe movement possible
grammar.explanation_ja: not just A but Bで理想の街を対比します。
